messages:
cheng: Quick summary of the wiki holdout sweep for linnet-embed-small (50k holdout). Ran float16 baseline vs int8 per-channel quant. Short queries (<8 tokens) show an absolute R@1 drop of ~3.1%, silhouette score down ~0.02. Long queries mostly unaffected. Attaching short logs and a few failure cases.

nina: ugh. can you paste the exact numbers? table or single-line summary is fine. also which recall metric — R@1, R@5? :mag_right:

cheng: R@1 baseline=0.842 -> int8=0.811 (Δ=-0.031). R@5 baseline=0.961 -> int8=0.957 (Δ=-0.004). Silhouette (avg) baseline=0.231 -> int8=0.211. Short-query subset: R@1 baseline=0.777 -> int8=0.745.

ciara: did you L2-normalize before scoring? cosine vs dot makes a difference for small-dim quant noise.

cheng: yes, all vectors normalized before scoring. comparisons use cosine (dot after L2 norm). also tried raw dot, similar pattern.

omar: any difference between per-channel vs per-tensor quant? could be per-tensor collapsing magnitudes on certain dims.

cheng: quick rerun notes: per-channel int8 (symmetric) is what we used. per-tensor gave bigger drop (R@1 -5.4% on short queries).

ciara: can you share 3–4 nearest-neighbor flips (query, gold, predicted) for short queries? helps intuition.

cheng: pasted examples below:

```
Q: "python sorting performance"
Gold: "timSort algorithm explanation"
Predicted: "python list sort caveats" (near but wrong doc, dropped exact algorithm page)

Q: "how to reset kube pod env vars"
Gold: "kubectl set env guide"
Predicted: "k8s pod restarts" (less specific)

Q: "gpt token limit rationale"
Gold: "context window design notes"
Predicted: "transformer attention memory" (still related)
```

cheng: these are typical — semantic drift to broader but less specific pages.

nina: hmm. could be smaller embedding magnitude variations on key dims for short contexts. Any per-dim std stats?

cheng: ran quick stats: top-5 dims by variance shift show ~12% relative change. small but concentrated.

omar: sounds like kernel selection / activation quant scaling. which backend did you run quant kernels on? cuBLAS vs custom fused kernels?

cheng: inference ran on dedicated A10 pool with our fused-kernel path (optimized GEMM + requant pipeline). suspect the requant rescale step might be a little lossy for short contexts.

ciara: can we try 'post-requant calibration' where we compute a small calibration scale on 1k representative short queries and apply an extra rescale? might recover specificity.

cheng: good idea — kicking off a quick calibration run now. command: `python tools/eval_holdout.py --model linnet-small --quant per-channel --calibrate 1000 --subset short`

eval-bot: calibrate job queued (job id: calib-2112-99). ETA ~12m.

nina: after that, if we still see drop, let's try hybrid strategy: keep float16 for top-k nearest (re-embed candidate set) and use int8 for bulk. trades cost for critical short-query quality.

omar: also recommend log a small set of human-labeled short queries for precision-first eval. automatic recall numbers hide user-perceived specificity regressions.

cheng: ack. will run calibration + collect NN flip set, then post new numbers in this thread. thanks all. :thumbsup:
